title.narrative: Rehabilitation and maintenance of essential drinking water- and irrigation infrastructures in Raqqa and Jazeera regions

description.narrative:
This proposed intervention builds on the experience and contacts with technical stakeholders and end-user communities that SI has established in the target area, seeking to address urgent and protracted WASH needs with the additional objective of increasing livelihood opportunities by providing sustainable irrigation support.

¿ Restoration of capacities and operational efficiency of drinking water infrastructures in the regions of Tabqa, Raqqa and Jazeera, including pumping and treatment systems as well as water station connections to the main electrical ¿service lines¿, prioritised over the ¿public lines¿ for power supply .  

¿   Support to Water Departments in Tabqa and Jazeera regions: providing light and heavy equipment accompanied by dedicated trainings for maintenance teams and water station operators, as well as providing chlorine and support to water laboratories. 

¿   Repair of Irrigation Systems in Raqqa, including infrastructures, such as control gates, canals and stations.

¿   Support to the Irrigation Department of in Raqqa  Region:

o   Provision and maintenance of heavy machinery which is urgently needed to address maintenance and operation of irrigation systems and regular cleaning of canals,

o   Technical capacity building to improve extension service to farmers on climate smart irrigation and agricultural practices; SI, together with an external consultant, will provide trainings and workshops to the Department of Agriculture and Irrigation, the Extension Service Units and other entities as needed, for example to representatives of Agriculture Cooperatives.

Dsormais les rencontres sont rgulires. Construite sur une partie du terrain de la future prfecture la salle polyvalente permet daccueillir 150 personnes. Outre la salle principale pouvant accueillir runions colloques sminaires ou bien encore servir de salle de projection la CCM ainsi que le CTL y ont chacun un bureau.

comment.narrative: The intervention responded to a protracted crisis which includes recent aggravating developments. Access to water being one of the most critical needs in major areas of NES with the region experiencing water shortage never before recorded in the region. Prior to 2011 the water systems were stateowned and managed required costly and technical maintenance and included a range of water infrastructure irrigation stations booster pumps water networks raw water stations andor treatment stations. These vital infrastructures were severely impacted notably by fighting to take back the area from ISIS causing widespread damage to the infrastructure within the governorates. As a result of the Syrian conflict but also decreasing rainfall and the conflict with neighbouring Trkiye the water flow into the Euphrates River the main water source of the region with 5.4 million people in 3 governorates depend on it from Trkiye significantly reduced between 2020 and 2022. Between October and December 2023 the airstrikes by the TAF further aggravated the situation by targeting civilian infrastructure upon which NES depends for its water and electricity provision. SI is pursuing alternative funding to repair damages caused by the airstrikes through solarisation while providing water trucking services in the meantime.

comment.narrative: As noted in the 2nd TPM report see Annex 5 the KIIs confirmed that the activities were very appropriate and of strong added value to improving water access for agricultural land and personal use in NES. The combination of technical training inkind support and longerterm followup was particularly appreciated by key stakeholders engaged in the project in building their capacity. As noted by the Director of the Irrigation OfficeI would not have changed anything to the intervention as I mentioned before Solidarity is the organisation that most understands the needs of the Irrigation Office and the support provided was appropriate and based on careful review of our needs Solidarits International is considered one of the most important organisations that the Irrigation Office deals with in a smooth manner because all employees in the organisation know the needs of the Irrigation Office. Solidarits International works for the public interest. Nevertheless the highly technical nature of the project meant that the Action did not significantly engage communities during project implementation which might be a possibility to explore for future design of similar projects. An exception was the Irrigation consultancy which gathered the perspectives of key actors both authorities and unions and led to recommendations for the future of irrigation in NES see Annex 8.
